claim: For every fixed grading exponent \(r>0\), the exact Manià energy of the nodal piecewise-affine interpolant of \(u_*(x)=x^{1/3}\) on \(x_i=(i/N)^r\) satisfies \(\mathcal I[I_N^{(r)}]=N^r\sum_{i=1}^N i^{-r}F(((i-1)/i)^r)\sim C_rN^r\), where \(F(\rho)=s(\rho)^6\int_\rho^1(\phi_\rho(t)^3-t)^2dt\), \(s(\rho)=(1-\rho^{1/3})/(1-\rho)\), \(\phi_\rho(t)=\rho^{1/3}+s(\rho)(t-\rho)\), and \(C_r=\sum_{i=1}^\infty i^{-r}F(((i-1)/i)^r)\in(0,\infty)\). In particular, \(\mathcal I[I_N^{(r)}]\ge(8/105)N^r\).

correctness.rationale: The cell substitution x=x_i t gives an exact identity for each cell and hence for the full energy. Taylor expansion of the interpolation error at t=1 yields F(rho)=(1-rho)^5/196830+O((1-rho)^6); because 1-((i-1)/i)^r=r/i+O(i^-2), the coefficient series has terms asymptotic to r^5/(196830 i^(r+5)) and converges for every fixed r>0. The first cell contributes exactly (8/105)N^r. Exact rational checks for r=3 and finite N are supplementary, not the all-r proof.

value.rationale: Endpoint grading is a standard numerical response to singular minimizers. This theorem gives a complete exact asymptotic family for every fixed power exponent and quantifies that grading alone does not remove the nodal interpolant's energy blow-up. The result is an analytic rate and coefficient, not merely a numerical experiment; its scope is deliberately limited to the specified interpolants.
